title: Isolation of Cancer Stem Cells by Sphere Formation Assay
author: Kwang Nickel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdt8i6rw

steps.title: Prepare sphere formation media
steps.instruction: Make 100 mL of sphere formation media by mixing DMEM/F12 with supplements: add 1 mL Penicillin‑Streptomycin, 2 mL B‑27, 20 µL basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF), 10 µL human EGF, and bring the final volume to 100 mL with DMEM/F12 (≈96.97 mL).

substeps.instruction: Measure 96.97 mL DMEM/F12 into a sterile container.
Add 1 mL Penicillin‑Streptomycin.
Add 2 mL B‑27 supplement.
Add 20 µL bFGF.
Add 10 µL hEGF.
Mix gently and bring volume to 100 mL if needed.

steps.title: Generate single-cell suspension and count
steps.instruction: Obtain a single‑cell suspension from cultured cells or primary tumor tissue, then count cells using a hemocytometer or automated counter.

substeps.instruction: Harvest cells from culture or tissue.
Dissociate to a single‑cell suspension (e.g., trypsinization, mechanical dissociation).
Resuspend cells in appropriate buffer.
Count viable cells and record total cell number.

steps.title: Dilute cells to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute the counted cells in the prepared sphere formation media to a final concentration of 2 000 cells · mL⁻¹ (optimize per cell line if needed).

steps.title: Plate cells in low‑attachment wells
steps.instruction: Add 250 µL of the cell suspension (≈500 cells) to each well of a 24‑well low‑attachment plate; do not use standard tissue‑culture plates.

substeps.instruction: Label the 24‑well low‑attachment plate.
Pipette 250 µL of the 2 000 cells/mL suspension into each well (≈500 cells per well).

steps.title: Incubate plates under controlled conditions
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a humidified incubator set to 95 % relative humidity, 37 °C, and 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Refresh media daily to maintain volume
steps.instruction: Check the plate each day and add fresh sphere formation media as needed to keep each well roughly 20 % filled, compensating for evaporation.

substeps.instruction: Inspect each well for volume loss.
Add sterile media to bring the well volume back to ~20 % of well capacity.

steps.title: Monitor and count spheres over time
steps.instruction: Examine wells under a microscope starting at 2 days, then daily; identify spheres ≥50 µm in diameter, and perform a final count (typically day 7).

substeps.instruction: At 2 days post‑plating, inspect each well and note any spheres ≥50 µm.
Continue daily observations.
Record the number of spheres per well each day.
Perform the final sphere count on day 7 (or as appropriate).

steps.title: Calculate sphere formation efficiency
steps.instruction: For each well, compute sphere formation efficiency (%) = (number of spheres ÷ number of cells seeded) × 100; repeat for at least three biological replicates and report the mean and standard deviation.

substeps.instruction: Apply the formula to each well’s data.
Average the efficiencies across replicates.
Calculate standard deviation.
Report the mean ± SD.
